clue.text: Put together advance to break plot

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a plot of ground for growing flowers is a bed
to advance money is to lend it

explanation.surface: Someone assembles a scheme by putting money into a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Things blended have been mixed and combined, which is what putting them together does.

clue.text: Clean up the Italian and German and US medical program

parts.note: la is the Italian feminine word for the
und is German for and
ER was an American hospital TV drama

explanation.surface: A list of national contributions to tidying up a US healthcare scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder is to wash clothes, or to clean up illicit money by passing it through legitimate channels.

clue.text: US city harbours a very quiet waste containment facility

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter within, so the city abbreviation surrounds the other letters

parts.note: NY is New York
taken as written
pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: An American city has a discreet sewage plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Nappy is the British word for a diaper; 'waste containment facility' is a mock-grand description of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A nappy (diaper) holds a baby's waste, so it is jokily a facility for containing it.

clue.text: When it's due, celebrity is about to come out

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: estimated time of arrival
a big name is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A star is about to make an appearance at the expected time.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source, a synonym for come out.

clue.text: Deceptively rich clothing for one going commando

definitions.text: Deceptively rich clothing for one going commando

parts.note: surface reading: a garment that makes its wearer look wealthier than they are
setter's reading: the British saying about an outfit worn with no knickers underneath

explanation.surface: A description of showy clothes worn by someone with no underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The British phrase 'fur coat and no knickers' describes someone who looks posh on the outside but lacks substance underneath; going commando means wearing no underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment in that British saying stands for a glamorous exterior hiding a lack of refinement beneath.

clue.text: In the middle of June, Swiss friends get silly

indicators.note: points to the central letters of each following word

parts.note: the two central letters
the three central letters
the central letter of seven

explanation.surface: Swiss friends start acting foolishly in midsummer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwise means showing poor judgement, which is what silly behaviour shows.

clue.text: Company pitch a line — this may be the result

parts.note: standard abbreviation
a ship pitches and rolls
taken as written
railway, a rail line

explanation.surface: A firm makes a sales pitch, with consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: A corollary is a proposition or consequence that follows naturally from another, a result.

clue.text: Sums made by relatives embracing a Latin way of working

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap around, so the relatives surround the Latin phrase

parts.note: aunts are relatives
modus operandi, Latin for a method of working

explanation.surface: Family members do arithmetic using a classical method.
explanation.definitionFit: Amounts are totals or quantities, so sums in the plural noun sense.

clue.text: Sad mainland loser? He was very successful at sea

definitions.text: He was very successful at sea

indicators.note: sad in its sense of sorry or in poor shape suggests the letters are in a bad state and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A defeated land-dweller is contrasted with a naval hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson was the British admiral who won the Battle of Trafalgar in 1805.

clue.text: Sound hesitant in signing for another quiz

indicators.note: the hesitation sound is placed inside the abbreviation for signing on behalf of another

parts.note: p.p. (per procurationem) is written when signing a letter on someone else's behalf
the noise a hesitant speaker makes

explanation.surface: Someone delegated to sign a document sounds unsure about a further test.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to question them persistently for information, a verb sense of quiz.

clue.text: Lady who ran distribution for artist …

indicators.note: distribution spreads things around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman managed the distribution of an artist's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy Warhol was the American pop artist famous for his soup-can and celebrity prints.

clue.text: … hired gymnasium, showing stuff that's avant garde

indicators.note: the words put their contents on display, so the letters are found inside the phrase

parts.note: found spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A rented gym puts on display some cutting-edge material.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to the artist in the clue before, though the two clues are independent.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy art is daring and unconventional, which is what being avant garde means.

clue.text: It's offensive ignoring Victor when in a bad way, financially

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: unable to pay one's debts
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Being broke is presented as an insult, minus one person.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove V from INSOLVENT to leave INSOLENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent behaviour is rude and disrespectful, the sense in which remarks are called offensive.

clue.text: Oscar called? Call back — he insists on marching

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
phoned

indicators.note: going back means the word for a call is read from right to left

parts.note: to call something is to name it

explanation.surface: Someone named Oscar phoned and is asked to ring back.
explanation.walkthrough: An Orangeman belongs to the Protestant Orange Order of Northern Ireland, famous for its annual marching parades.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Orange Order hold traditional marches each July and insist on their right to parade.

clue.text: Wrong moment to go after rising criminal, admitting nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word reads upward, so it is reversed

parts.note: a con is a convict

indicators.note: the letters are wrongly ordered and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bad time for a convict to be pursued, while confessing to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: 'No comment' is the stock reply of someone declining to admit anything, as suspects say under questioning.

clue.text: Spoil quiet swamp

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone ruins a peaceful wetland.
explanation.definitionFit: A marsh is low waterlogged ground, a synonym for swamp.

clue.text: Knock over playground equipment? Sounds a bit rude

indicators.note: says the answer is heard as the spoken form of the turned-round words

parts.note: a see-saw with its two halves turned over

explanation.surface: A child topples a piece of playground kit, and it sounds a little naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: Knocking over the see-saw swaps its two syllables, and 'saw-see' said aloud is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saucy means cheekily suggestive, so mildly rude in a playful way.

clue.text: Varied characters Croat actor played, for example

definitions.meaning: first meaning: letters rearranged into a new order
second meaning: Croat is a rearrangement of actor, an instance of the device

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a Croatian performer in many roles; in fact the five letters of 'Croat' are those of 'actor' reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a word formed by reordering another word's letters, as Croat is from actor.

clue.text: Your howl about importing nitrogen causes major dispute

indicators.note: importing brings something in, so the element is taken inside the other letters
about suggests moving things around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Someone's loud complaint about bringing in nitrogen starts a big argument.
explanation.definitionFit: An unholy row is an idiom for a furious quarrel, unholy acting as an intensifier.

clue.text: Legend upset by article describing old empire

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a legend can be an inscription or motto
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An ancient myth disturbed by a newspaper piece about a historic realm.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ottoman Empire was the Turkish empire that lasted from around 1300 to 1922.

clue.text: Fury when abandoning run leads to power loss

indicators.note: the answer, on abandoning a letter, leads to another word, so that letter must be put back inside it

parts.note: a power outage is a loss of electricity supply
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Anger as a dropped run causes a blackout.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay works backwards: the answer minus R gives OUTAGE, so R goes into OUTAGE to build it.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is intense anger, a synonym for fury.

clue.text: Passion of East Ender trying to sound more tough

indicators.note: points to how the word is pronounced in a particular accent

parts.words: East Ender trying to sound more tough
parts.note: a Cockney drops the h of harder

explanation.surface: A Londoner keen to appear tougher shows great passion.
explanation.walkthrough: An East Ender is a Cockney from London's East End, whose accent drops initial h, so 'harder' becomes 'arder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is intense enthusiasm or love, a synonym for passion.

clue.text: Where royalty may get comfort, it's said

definitions.text: Where royalty may get comfort, it's said

parts.note: a soothing ointment, hence comfort
something said is spoken, oral

explanation.surface: A royal residence is a place of comfort, or so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the castle is described as where royals find comfort. Balmoral is the royal family's castle in Aberdeenshire, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral Castle is the private Scottish retreat where the British royal family relaxes in summer.

clue.text: Finish off job quickly but lose some information

indicators.note: the finish of each word is taken off it, so only its closing letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Rushing to complete a task means some data goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A byte is a unit of digital data, eight bits, so a small amount of information.

clue.text: Something obscure on book may help to sell it

parts.note: something blurred is indistinct
B is a standard abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: An unclear note on a book's cover can still help it sell.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: publicity text printed on a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is the promotional text on a book's jacket, written to persuade people to buy it.

clue.text: As expected, not betraying class

definitions.meaning: first meaning: behaving in the usual, predictable way
second meaning: staying loyal to one's form, a school class

explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group, so being true to it means not betraying classmates.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting characteristically; read literally it means being faithful to a form, a school class.

clue.text: Urgent approach when evacuating large part of the US

indicators.note: evacuating empties out the words, leaving only their outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: An urgent approach is needed when clearing people out of a big region of America.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is a large western state of the United States.

clue.text: Conservative type on warm day regularly becomes passionate

indicators.note: in an across answer, placed on means coming after, so the party member goes second
at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A stuffy right-winger warms up on a hot day.
explanation.definitionFit: Amatory means relating to sexual love, so it describes passionate feeling.

clue.text: Clever clogs finish up, when permitted

indicators.note: to clog is to block up, filling the inside of the other word

parts.note: a finish is an end
able means capable or clever

explanation.surface: A know-all is allowed to finish things off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clever clogs' looks like the British phrase for a smart alec, but clogs is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Enabled means given the means or permission to do something, so allowed.
